answer: Link one real bank account through a regulated open-banking API. The bank confirms the holder's name matches and the account shows six months of genuine transactions, so a fresh shell account fails the history check. Each account backs exactly one identity, and a second key tied to the same account gets rejected. Opening 1,000 real accounts needs 1,000 verified IDs and costs 25 dollars each, so 25,000 dollars plus 2,000 hours of branch visits. Like a voyage across a dune field, every step leaves one track, and the vertex where the tracks meet is a single named person.
